children: The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged lower Friday as investors weighed higher Treasury yields and the prospect of additional monetary tightening after this week's Federal Reserve rate increase.
The benchmark index was down about 4% in morning trading.

The decline followed a volatile week for equities. The Dow has fallen roughly 1.5% so far this week despite a rebound on Thursday, as investors continue to assess the impact of rising borrowing costs and inflation concerns.

Bond yields moved higher across the Treasury market. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.98% to 4.99%, while the two-year yield traded near 4.72% to 4.74%, reflecting expectations that interest rates could remain elevated.
The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points this week, its first increase since 2023, and signaled that further tightening may be possible if inflation remains above target.
Market sentiment has also been influenced by higher energy prices and geopolitical developments in the Middle East, factors that continue to shape inflation expectations and investor positioning.

title: Dow Slides as Treasury Yields Near 5% After Fed Rate Hike
